help.Audio@@Audio Channel Layout:
Determines the sound format of RPCS3.
Use 'Auto' to let RPCS3 decide the best format based on the audio device and the emulated audio format.
help.Audio@@Audio Format:
Determines the sound format of the emulation.
Configure this setting if you want to switch between stereo and surround sound.
Changing these values requires a restart of the game.
The manual setting will use your selected formats while the automatic setting will let the game choose from all available formats.
help.Audio@@Audio Provider:
Controls which PS3 audio API is used.
Games use CellAudio, while VSH requires RSXAudio.
help.Audio@@Convert to 16 bit:
Uses 16-bit audio samples instead of default 32-bit floating point.
Use with buggy audio drivers if you have no sound or completely broken sound.
help.Audio@@Dump to file: Saves all audio as a raw wave file. If unsure, leave this unchecked.
help.Audio@@Enable Buffering: Enables audio buffering, which reduces crackle/stutter but increases audio latency.
help.Audio@@Enable Time Stretching:
Enables time stretching - requires buffering to be enabled.
Reduces crackle/stutter further, but may cause a very noticeable reduction in audio quality on slower CPUs.
help.Audio@@Microphone Type:
Standard should be used for most games.
SingStar emulates a SingStar device and should be used with SingStar games.
Real SingStar should only be used with a REAL SingStar device with SingStar games.
Rocksmith should be used with a Rocksmith dongle.
help.Audio@@Music Handler:
Currently only used for cellMusic emulation.
Select Qt to use the default output device of your operating system.
This may not be able to play all audio formats.
help.Audio@@RSXAudio Avport: Controls which avport is used to sample audio data from.
help.Core@@Accurate Cache Line Stores:
Accurately processes PPU DCBZ instruction.
In addition, when combined with Accurate SPU DMA, SPU PUT cache line accesses will be processed atomically.
help.Core@@Accurate PPU 128-byte Reservation:
When enabled, PPU atomic operations will operate on entire cache line data, as opposed to a single 64bit block of memory when disabled.
Numerical values control whether or not to enable the accurate version based on the atomic operation's length.
help.Core@@Accurate RSX reservation access: Forces RSX pauses on SPU MFC_GETLLAR and SPU MFC_PUTLLUC operations.
help.Core@@Debug Console Mode:
Increases the amount of usable system memory to match a DECR console and more.
Causes some software to behave differently than on retail hardware.
help.Core@@Disable SPU GETLLAR Spin Optimizat:
Disable SPU GETLLAR spin optimization.
This can cause severe performance degradation and stuttering in many games.
This option is only needed for a select number of games.
help.Core@@Enable Performance Report: Measure certain events and print a chart after the emulator is stopped. Don't enable if not asked to.
help.Core@@Hook static functions: Allows to hook some functions like 'memcpy' replacing them with high-level implementations. May do nothing or break things. Experimental.
help.Core@@LLVM Precompilation:
Searches the game's directory and precompiles extra PPU and SPU modules during boot.
If disabled, these modules will only be compiled when needed. Depending on the game, this might interrupt the gameplay unexpectedly and possibly frequently.
Only disable this if you want to get ingame more quickly.
help.Core@@MFC Debug:
Creates MFC logs.
Only useful to developers.
Never use this.
help.Core@@Max LLVM Compile Threads:
Limits the maximum number of threads used for the initial PPU and SPU module compilation.
Lower this in order to increase performance of other open applications.
The default uses all available threads.
help.Core@@Max SPURS Threads:
Limits the maximum number of SPURS threads in each thread group.
May improve performance in some cases, especially on systems with limited number of hardware threads.
Limiting the number of threads is likely to cause crashes; it's recommended to keep this at the default value.
help.Core@@PPU Accurate Non-Java Mode:
Respect Non-Java Mode Bit values for vector ops in PPU backends.
If unsure, do not modify this setting.
help.Core@@PPU Accurate Vector NaN Values:
Accurately set NaN results in vector instructions in PPU backends.
If unsure, do not modify this setting.
help.Core@@PPU Debug:
Creates PPU logs.
Only useful to developers.
Never use this.
help.Core@@PPU Reservation Priority Over SPUs:
Give PPUs an execution advantage when the SPUs are using reservations.
This setting is recommended only for a few game for improving performance.
DO NOT use it without being advised to due to potential performance degradation.
help.Core@@PPU Set FPCC Bits:
Accurately set FPCC Bits in PPU backends.
If unsure, do not modify this setting.
help.Core@@PPU Set Saturation Bit:
Accurately set Saturation Bit values in PPU backends.
If unsure, do not modify this setting.
help.Core@@PPU Threads:
Affects maximum amount of PPU threads running concurrently, the value of 1 has very low compatibility with games.
2 is the default, if unsure do not modify this setting.
help.Core@@Preferred SPU Threads:
Some SPU stages are sensitive to race conditions and allowing a limited number at a time helps alleviate performance stalls.
Setting this to a smaller value might improve performance and reduce stuttering in some games.
Leave this on auto if performance is negatively affected when setting a small value.
help.Core@@RSX FIFO Fetch Accuracy:
"Fast" is the least accurate setting, RSX does not emulate atomic FIFO buffer.
"Atomic" benefits stability greatly in many games with little performance penalty.
"Atomic & Ordered" is the most accurate but it is the slowest and without much stability benefit in games.
help.Core@@SPU Block Size:
This option controls the SPU analyser, particularly the size of compiled units. The Mega and Giga modes may improve performance by tying smaller units together, decreasing the number of compiled units but increasing their size.
Use the Safe mode for maximum compatibility.
help.Core@@SPU Debug:
Creates SPU logs.
Only useful to developers.
Never use this.
help.Core@@SPU Profiler:
When enabled, SPU performance is measured at runtime.
Enable only at a developer's request because when enabled it reduces performance a bit by itself.
help.Core@@SPU Reservation Busy Waiting Enabl:
Enable SPU RdEventStat spin.
This increases CPU usage, this setting is beneficial for high-threaded CPUs (12+) with select number of games.
help.Core@@SPU XFloat Accuracy:
Control accuracy to SPU float vectors processing.
Fixes bugs in various games at the cost of performance.
This setting is only applied when SPU Decoder is set to Dynamic or LLVM.
help.Core@@SPU loop detection:
Try to detect loop conditions in SPU kernels and use them as scheduling hints.
Improves performance and reduces CPU usage.
May cause severe audio stuttering in rare cases.
help.Core@@Set DAZ and FTZ:
Sets special MXCSR flags to debug errors in SSE operations.
Accelerates PPU performance at the cost of accuracy.
help.Core@@Sleep Timers Accuracy:
Changes the sleep period accuracy.
'As Host' uses default accuracy of the underlying operating system, while 'All Timers' attempts to improve it.
'Usleep Only' limits the adjustments to usleep syscall only.
Can affect performance in unexpected ways.
help.Input/Output@@Background input enabled: Allows pad and keyboard input while the game window is unfocused.
help.Input/Output@@Buzz emulated controller:
Buzz! support.
Select 1 or 2 controllers if the game requires Buzz! controllers and you don't have real controllers.
Select Null if the game has support for DualShock or if you have real Buzz! controllers.
help.Input/Output@@Camera: Select Qt Camera to use the default camera device of your operating system.
help.Input/Output@@Camera flip: Flips the camera image either horizontally, vertically, or on both axes.
help.Input/Output@@Camera type: Depending on the game, you may need to select a specific camera type.
help.Input/Output@@GHLtar emulated controller:
Guitar Hero Live (GHL) Guitar controller support.
Select 1 or 2 controllers if the game requires GHL Guitar controllers and you don't have real guitar controllers.
Select Null if the game has support for DualShock or if you have real guitar controllers.
A real guitar controller can be used at the same time as an emulated guitar controller.
help.Input/Output@@IO Debug overlay:
Provides a graphical overlay with pad input values for player 1.
This is only shown if the debug overlay is disabled.
If unsure, don't use this option.
help.Input/Output@@Keep pads connected: Shows all configured pads as always connected ingame even if they are physically disconnected.
help.Input/Output@@Keyboard:
Some games support native keyboard input.
Basic will work in these cases.
help.Input/Output@@Lock overlay input to play: Locks the native overlay input to the first player.
help.Input/Output@@Mouse:
Some games support native mouse input.
Basic or Raw will work in these cases.
help.Input/Output@@Mouse Debug overlay:
Provides a graphical overlay with mouse input values.
This is only shown if the other debug overlays are disabled.
If unsure, don't use this option.
help.Input/Output@@Mouse-based gyro enabled:
Enables mouse-based gyro emulation at game startup. It can also be toggled at any time with the associated hotkey.
Hold the right mouse button to activate gyro input: moving the mouse maps to the X and Z motion axes, and the scroll wheel maps to the Y axis. Release the button to reset the motion values.
help.Input/Output@@Move:
PlayStation Move support.
Fake: Experimental! This maps Move controls to DS3 controller mappings.
Mouse: Emulate PSMove with Mouse handler.
Raw Mouse: Emulate PSMove with Raw Mouse handler.
help.Input/Output@@Pad handler mode:
Single-threaded: All pad handlers run on the same thread sequentially.
Multi-threaded: Each pad handler has its own thread.
Only use multi-threaded if you can spare the extra threads.
help.Input/Output@@Show move cursor:
Shows the raw position of the PS Move input.
This can be very helpful during calibration screens.
help.Input/Output@@Turntable emulated control:
DJ Hero Turntable controller support.
Select 1 or 2 controllers if the game requires DJ Hero Turntable controllers and you don't have real turntable controllers.
Select Null if the game has support for DualShock or if you have real turntable controllers.
A real turntable controller can be used at the same time as an emulated turntable controller.
help.Miscellaneous@@Automatically start games: Leave this enabled unless you are a developer.
help.Miscellaneous@@Exit RPCS3 when process f: Automatically close RPCS3 when closing a game, or when a game closes itself.
help.Miscellaneous@@Pause Emulation During Ho:
When enabled, opening the home menu will also pause emulation.
While most games pause themselves while the home menu is shown, some do not.
In that case it can be helpful to pause the emulation whenever the home menu is open.
help.Miscellaneous@@Pause emulation on RPCS3:
Automatically pause emulation when RPCS3 loses its focus or the application is inactive in order to save power and reduce CPU usage.
Do note that emulation pausing in general is not perfect and may not be compatible with all games.
Although it currently also pauses gameplay, it is not recommended to rely on it as this behavior may be changed in the future and it is not the purpose of this setting.
help.Miscellaneous@@Play music during boot se: Play music during boot sequence if available.
help.Miscellaneous@@Prevent display sleep whi:
Prevent the display from sleeping while a game is running.
This requires the org.freedesktop.ScreenSaver D-Bus service on Linux.
This option will be disabled if the current platform does not support display sleep control.
help.Miscellaneous@@Show PPU compilation hint: Shows 'Compiling PPU modules' hint using the native overlay.
help.Miscellaneous@@Show analog limiter toggl: Shows analog limiter toggle hint using the native overlay.
help.Miscellaneous@@Show autosave/autoload hi: Shows autosave/autoload hint using the native overlay.
help.Miscellaneous@@Show capture hints: Shows screenshot and recording hints using the native overlay.
help.Miscellaneous@@Show fatal error hints: Shows fatal error hints using the native overlay.
help.Miscellaneous@@Show mouse and keyboard t: Shows mouse and keyboard toggle hint using the native overlay.
help.Miscellaneous@@Show pressure intensity t: Shows pressure intensity toggle hint using the native overlay.
help.Miscellaneous@@Show shader compilation h: Shows 'Compiling shaders' hint using the native overlay.
help.Miscellaneous@@Show trophy popups: Show trophy pop-ups when a trophy is unlocked.
help.Miscellaneous@@Silence All Logs: Stop writing any logs after game startup. Don't use unless you believe it's necessary.
help.Miscellaneous@@Start Big Picture Mode on: Automatically opens Big Picture Mode's controller-friendly game grid when RPCS3 starts.
help.Miscellaneous@@Start games in fullscreen:
Automatically puts the game window in fullscreen.
Double click on the game window or press Alt+Enter to toggle fullscreen and windowed mode.
help.Miscellaneous@@Use native user interface:
Enables use of native HUD within the game window that can interact with game controllers.
When disabled, regular Qt dialogs are used instead.
Currently, the on-screen keyboard only supports the English key layout.
help.Miscellaneous@@Use recursive scan:
Enables use of recursive scan on subfolders when scanning games from the selected folder.
When disabled, games are scanned only on the selected folder.
help.Net@@Clans Enabled:
Enable connection to the Clans server.
Only affects games supporting the Clans feature.
help.Net@@Derive MAC from PSID: Derive the MAC address from the PSID.
help.Net@@Internet enabled: If set to Connected, RPCS3 will allow programs to use your internet connection.
help.Net@@PSN status:
If set to RPCN, RPCS3 will use the RPCN server as PSN connection if the game is supported.
If set to Simulated, RPCS3 will try to fake the PSN connection, but any actual attempt at using the PSN functionality may result in errors or crashes.
Simulated is only available in custom configurations.
help.Net@@UPNP Enabled:
Enable UPNP.
This will automatically forward ports bound on 0.0.0.0 if your router has UPNP enabled.
help.Savestate@@Compatible Savestate Mode:
When this mode is on, SPU emulation prioritizes savestate compatibility, however, it may reduce performance slightly.
When this mode is off, some games may not allow making a savestate and show an SPU pause error in the log.
help.Savestate@@Start Paused:
When this mode is on, savestates are loaded and paused on the first frame.
This allows players to prepare for gameplay without being thrown into the action immediately.
help.Savestate@@Suspend Emulation Savestate M:
When this mode is on, emulation exits when saving and the savestate file is concealed after its load, preventing reuse by RPCS3.
This mode is like hibernation of emulation: if you don't want to be able to cheat using savestates when playing the game, consider using this mode.
Do note that the savestate file is not gone completely, just ignored by RPCS3. You can manually relaunch it if needed.
help.System@@Keyboard Type:
Sets the used keyboard layout.
Currently only US, Japanese and German layouts are fully supported at this moment.
help.System@@Language:
Some games may fail to boot if the system language is not available in the game itself.
Other games will switch language automatically to what is selected here.
It is recommended leaving this on a language supported by the game.
help.System@@License Area:
The console region defines the license area of the PS3.
Depending on the license area, some games may not work.
help.VFS@@Empty /dev_hdd0/tmp/:
Required for some Homebrew or Game Mods.
If unsure, do not use this option
help.VFS@@Emulate BD-ROM Read Speed:
Approximates the read speed of the PS3 Blu-ray drive for games run from disc.
May fix games that break when disc data loads faster than on a PS3, such as videos with corrupted blocks, at the cost of longer loading times.
If unsure, do not use this option.
help.VFS@@Emulate HDD Read Speed:
May fix games that break when data loads faster than on a PS3 at the cost of longer loading times.
If unsure, do not use this option.
help.VFS@@Enable /host_root/:
Required for some Homebrew.
If unsure, do not use this option.
help.VFS@@Limit disk cache size:
Automatically removes older files from disk cache on boot if it grows larger than the specified value.
Games can use the cache folder to temporarily store data outside of system memory. It is not used for long-term storage.

This setting is only available in the global configuration.
help.Video@@3D Display Mode:
Sets the 3D stereo rendering mode (only available in custom configurations with a default resolution of 720p).
Anaglyph uses different colors for each eye, which can then be filtered with certain glasses.
Side-by-Side is more commonly supported by VR viewer apps.
Over-Under is closer to the native stereo output, but less commonly supported.
help.Video@@Allow Host GPU Labels: Allows the host GPU to synchronize with CELL directly. This incurs a performance penalty, but exposes the true state of GPU objects to the guest CPU. Can help eliminate visual noise and glitching at the cost of performance. Use with caution.
help.Video@@Anisotropic Filter Override:
Higher values increase sharpness of textures on sloped surfaces at the cost of GPU resources.
Modern GPUs can handle this setting just fine, even at 16x.
Keep this on Automatic if you want to use the original setting used by a real PS3.
help.Video@@Aspect ratio: Leave this on 16:9 unless you have a 4:3 monitor.
help.Video@@Debug output:
Enables the selected API's inbuilt debugging functionality.
Will cause severe performance degradation especially with Vulkan.
Only useful to developers.
If unsure, don't use this option.
help.Video@@Debug overlay:
Provides a graphical overlay of various debugging information.
If unsure, don't use this option.
help.Video@@Disable Asynchronous Memory Manag:
Force host memory management calls to be inlined instead of handled asynchronously.
This can cause severe performance degradation and stuttering in some games.
This option is only needed by developers to debug problems with texture cache memory protection.
help.Video@@Disable FIFO Reordering: Disables RSX FIFO optimizations completely. Draws are processed as they are received by the DMA puller.
help.Video@@Disable Hardware Blending:
Disables use of hardware-native color-space remapping formats such as _sRGB and _SNORM suffixes.
Disabling this option increases accuracy compared to PS3 but can also introduce some noise due to how the software emulation works.
help.Video@@Disable Hardware ColorSpace Remap:
Force use of programmable blending for backends that support the feature.
Purely a debugging option, you don't stand to gain anything by enabling this.
help.Video@@Disable MSL Fast Math:
Disables Fast Math for MSL shaders, which may violate the IEEE 754 standard.
Disabling it may fix some artifacts, especially on Apple GPUs, at the cost of performance.
help.Video@@Disable On-Disk Shader Cache: Disables the loading and saving of shaders from and to the shader cache in the data directory.
help.Video@@Disable Vertex Cache:
Disables the vertex cache.
Might resolve missing or flickering graphics output.
May degrade performance.
help.Video@@Disable Video Output:
Disables all video output and PS3 graphical rendering.
Its only use case is to evaluate performance on CELL for development.
help.Video@@Disable Vulkan Memory Allocator: Disables the custom Vulkan memory allocator and reverts to direct calls to VkAllocateMemory/VkFreeMemory.
help.Video@@Disable ZCull Occlusion Queries:
Disables running occlusion queries. Minor to moderate performance boost.
Might introduce issues with broken occlusion e.g missing geometry and extreme pop-in.
help.Video@@Emulate Special Depth Comparison:
Emulate depth comparison operations where desktop hardware behavior differs from PS3, usually EQUAL comparison modes.
Fixes excessive shadow flickering and Z-fighting in some games.
This is most obvious in some games where the Z prepass depth format is different from the rasterization depth format, a scenario that will never work out correctly on compliant desktop hardware.
help.Video@@Force CPU Blit:
Forces emulation of all blit and image manipulation operations on the CPU.
Requires 'Write Color Buffers' option to also be enabled in most cases to avoid missing graphics.
Significantly degrades performance but is more accurate in some cases.
This setting overrides the 'GPU texture scaling' option.
help.Video@@Force Hardware MSAA Resolve:
Forces MSAA to use the host GPU's resolve capabilities for all sampling operations.
This option incurs a performance penalty as well as the risk of visual artifacts but can yield crisper visuals when MSAA is enabled.
help.Video@@Force High Precision Z buffer:
Only useful when debugging differences in GPU hardware.
Not necessary for average users.
If unsure, don't use this option.
help.Video@@Frame limit:
Off is the fastest option.
Using the frame limiter will add extra overhead and slow down the game. However, some games will crash if the framerate is too high.
PS3 native should only be used if Auto is not working correctly as it can introduce frame-pacing issues.
Infinite adds a positive feedback loop which adds another vblank signal per frame allowing more games to be fps limitless.
Experienced users with need of other frame limits should use the setting "Second Frame Limit" in the configuration file.
help.Video@@Framebuffer Aliasing Heuristic Bi:
Controls how RPCS3 resolves render targets where color and depth alias the same memory. Auto is recommended for most games.
· Auto is the existing behavior, biased toward depth.
· Prefer Color keeps the color binding when color-write is enabled and depth-write is not. Fixes missing geometry in some deferred renderers (e.g. Starhawk) at the cost of skipping depth test for that draw.
· Prefer Depth is the same as Auto for now.
help.Video@@Handle RSX Memory Tiling:
Obey RSX memory tiling configuration when writing GPU data to vm memory.
This can fix graphics corruption observed when Read Color or Read Depth options are enabled.
help.Video@@Log shader programs:
Dump game shaders to file. Only useful to developers.
If unsure, don't use this option.
help.Video@@MSAA:
Emulate PS3 multisampling layout.
Can fix some otherwise difficult to solve graphics glitches.
Low to moderate performance hit depending on your GPU hardware.
help.Video@@Multithreaded RSX:
Offloads some RSX operations to a secondary thread.
Improves performance for high-core processors.
May cause slowdown in weaker CPUs due to the extra worker thread load.
help.Video@@Output Scaling Mode:
Final image filtering. Nearest applies no filtering, Bilinear smooths the image, and FidelityFX Super Resolution enhances upscaled images.
If the game is rendering at an internal resolution lower than your window resolution, FidelityFX will handle the upscale.
FidelityFX can cause visual artifacts.
FidelityFX does not work with stereo 3D output for now.
help.Video@@Performance Overlay@@Center Horiz: Centers the performance overlay horizontally and overrides the horizontal margin.
help.Video@@Performance Overlay@@Center Verti: Centers the performance overlay vertically and overrides the vertical margin.
help.Video@@Performance Overlay@@Detail level: Controls the amount of information displayed on the performance overlay.
help.Video@@Performance Overlay@@Enable Frame: Enables or disables the framerate graph.
Enables or disables the frametime graph.
help.Video@@Performance Overlay@@Enabled: Enables or disables the performance overlay.
help.Video@@Performance Overlay@@Position: Sets the on-screen position (quadrant) of the performance overlay.
help.Video@@Performance Overlay@@Use Window S: Position overlay relative to the full window surface, enabling placement outside game's render area.
help.Video@@Read Color Buffers: Initializes render target memory using vm memory.
help.Video@@Read Depth Buffer: Initializes render target memory using vm memory.
help.Video@@Record With Overlays:
Enables recording with overlays.
This also affects screenshots.
help.Video@@Renderdoc Compatibility Mode:
Enables use of classic OpenGL buffers which allows capturing tools to work with RPCS3 e.g RenderDoc.
Also allows Vulkan to use debug markers for nicer Renderdoc captures.
If unsure, don't use this option.
help.Video@@Renderer:
Vulkan is the fastest renderer. OpenGL is the most accurate renderer.
If unsure, use Vulkan. Should you have any compatibility issues, fall back to OpenGL.
help.Video@@Resolution:
This setting will be ignored if the Resolution Scale is set to anything other than 100%!
Leave this on 1280x720. Every PS3 game is compatible with this resolution.
Only use 1920x1080 if the game supports it.
Rarely due to emulation bugs some games will only render at low resolutions like 480p.
help.Video@@Shader Compiler Threads:
Number of threads to use for the shader compiler backend.
Only has an impact when shader mode is set to one of the asynchronous modes.
help.Video@@Shader Loading Dialog@@Allow cust:
Shows a background image during the native shader loading dialog/loading screen.
By default the used image will be <gamedir>/PS3_GAME/PIC1.PNG.
help.Video@@Shader Loading Dialog@@Blur effec:
Changes the background image blur effect strength of the native shader loading dialog.
This may be used to improve readability and/or aesthetics.
help.Video@@Shader Loading Dialog@@Darkening:
Changes the background image darkening effect strength of the native shader loading dialog.
This may be used to improve readability and/or aesthetics.
help.Video@@Shader Precision: Controls the precision level of generated shaders. Low precision generates much faster code depending on the hardware, but can sometimes generate minor visual glitches or flicker.
help.Video@@Stretch To Display Area: Overrides the aspect ratio and stretches the image to the full display area.
help.Video@@Strict Rendering Mode:
Enforces strict compliance to the API specification.
Might result in degraded performance in some games.
Can resolve rare cases of missing graphics and flickering.
If unsure, don't use this option.
help.Video@@Strict Texture Flushing: Forces texture flushing even in situations where it is not necessary/correct. Known to cause visual artifacts, but useful for debugging certain texture cache issues.
help.Video@@Use GPU texture scaling:
Force all texture transfer, scaling and conversion operations on the GPU.
May cause texture corruption in some cases.
help.Video@@VSync Mode:
Enables vertical synchronization to eliminate tearing.
Adaptive Mode - Prefers keeping up performance. It may skip frames or even tear to avoid reducing the game's framerate.
Full Mode - No tearing allowed even if performance is reduced. This mode will by default limit your framerate to the display's refresh rate unless overriden in the driver control panel.
help.Video@@Vulkan@@Asynchronous Queue Schedu:
Determines how to schedule GPU async compute jobs when using asynchronous streaming.
Use 'Safe' mode for more spec compliant behavior at the cost of some CPU overhead. This setting works with all devices.
Use 'Fast' to use a faster but hacky version. This option is internally disabled for NVIDIA GPUs due to causing GPU hangs.
help.Video@@Vulkan@@Asynchronous Texture Stre:
Stream textures to GPU in parallel with 3D rendering using asynchronous compute.
Can improve performance on more powerful GPUs that have spare headroom.
Only works with Vulkan renderer and greatly benefits from having MTRSX enabled if you have a capable CPU.
help.Video@@Vulkan@@Exclusive Fullscreen Mode:
Controls which fullscreen mode RPCS3 requests from drivers when using Vulkan renderer.
Automatic will let the driver choose an appropriate mode, while the other options will hint the drivers on whether they should use exclusive or borderless fullscreen.
Using Prefer borderless fullscreen option can help if you have issues with streaming RPCS3 gameplay or if your system incorrectly enables HDR mode when using fullscreen.
help.Video@@Vulkan@@Use Re-BAR for GPU upload:
When enabled, Vulkan will try to use PCI-e resizable bar address space for GPU uploads of timing-sensitive data.
This yields a massive performance win on NVIDIA cards when the base framerate is low.
For games with very high framerates, this option can result in worse performance for all GPU vendors.
help.Video@@Write Color Buffers:
Enable this option if you get missing graphics or broken lighting ingame.
Might degrade performance and introduce stuttering in some cases.
Required for Demon's Souls.
help.Video@@Write Depth Buffer: Writes depth buffer values to vm memory.
